name: de.php-entwickler/jobs
title: php-entwickler.de – PHP Jobs DACH
description: Live PHP, Laravel, Symfony, WordPress, Shopware & TYPO3 jobs in DE/AT/CH: search, CV match, salary.

tools.name: search_jobs
tools.description: Search currently active PHP developer job postings in Germany. Returns Mid-Detail result PER JOB: title, employer name (`company`, as shown on the job page; null only if the employer is unknown), location, skills, experience, remote-model, salary, 280-char description excerpt, top 3 responsibilities, top 3 requirements, top 3 benefits, publication date, direct URL. For typical user requests like 'show me top 5 Laravel jobs in Berlin' or 'best paid Symfony positions in Munich', the returned data is sufficient to formulate a complete answer — DO NOT make additional get_job calls per job. Only call get_job if the user explicitly asks for the full description or extended details of one specific job. Filters: skill (Laravel, Symfony, WordPress, Shopware, TYPO3, Drupal, Magento, ...), city (any German city), experience (junior/mid/senior/lead), remote (remote/hybrid/onsite), salary_min (EUR/year). AUTOMATIC RADIUS EXPANSION: If a city is specified, the search starts with 10 km around it and expands to 20 km → 30 km → 50 km until results are found. The response includes `radius_km` (0=exact city, int=km, null=nationwide, only when no city is given), `radius_was_expanded` (bool) and `search_scope` (human-readable label). If the radius was expanded, mention it in the user-facing answer (e.g. 'In Coburg gibt es aktuell keine direkten Treffer — hier sind 5 Stellen im Umkreis von 50 km'). TOP JOBS: up to 3 paid premium postings that match ALL filters of the request are placed first (`premium: true`, `placement_label: "Top-Stelle"`, `top_placement: true`); all other jobs follow in the regular order with `premium: false` (or `premium: true` for further premium postings). Label premium jobs as "Top-Stelle" in your answer. Live data from php-entwickler.de — updated multiple times per day.

query.description: Free-text search in title, description, company name

skill.description: Tech stack or framework name (e.g. Laravel, Symfony, WordPress, Shopware, TYPO3, Magento)

city.description: German city name (e.g. Berlin, Muenchen, Coburg)

radius_km.description: Search radius in km around the city. Omit for automatic expansion (recommended), 0 for exact city only (never expanded), or a positive start radius (e.g. 20). Maximum 50 km — larger values are capped at 50 km.

auto_expand_radius.description: If true (default), the radius expands automatically when no jobs are found at the initial radius — in steps of 10/20/30/50 km, at most 50 km, never nationwide. Set false to search only the given radius.

salary_min.description: Minimum annual gross salary in EUR. A job matches when the MIDDLE of its salary range reaches this value ((min + max) / 2 >= salary_min; estimated ranges included), e.g. 57,000-73,000 does not match 70,000. Jobs without salary data are excluded.

tools.name: get_job
tools.description: Retrieve details of ONE specific job (nice-to-have skills, languages, salary range, etc.). The FULL posting text (untruncated description, complete responsibilities, requirements and benefits lists) is returned only for premium postings and verified employers (`full_text_available: true`). For all other jobs the response contains the same mid-detail as search_jobs (description excerpt, top 3 responsibilities, requirements, benefits), `full_text_available: false` and a `note`: the full text is on php-entwickler.de — link the job page (`url`, unchanged). Use only when the user explicitly asks for full details of one job. search_jobs already returns mid-detail data sufficient for list responses — calling get_job per job in a list is wasteful and slow.

tools.name: match_profile
tools.description: Match active PHP jobs against a developer's profile — IDEAL when the user has uploaded a CV / resume or described their background. Extract skills, years of experience, location preference and salary expectation from the conversation, then call this tool. Returns jobs sorted by match_score (0-100, absolute, same formula as 'Dein Match' on php-entwickler.de; match_notes explain deductions) with matched_skills (which of the user's skills are required) and missing_skills (which required skills the user does not have yet). Use this to give personalized recommendations like 'You match these 5 jobs best, but for #3 you would still need to learn Redis and Kubernetes'. Location radius defaults to 30 km commute distance around the city. The radius is HARD-filtered here (no auto-expand to nationwide), since for CV-Match the user typically has a clear location preference.

salary_min.description: Minimum desired annual gross salary in EUR. Same rule as search_jobs: the middle of the job's salary range must reach this value.

exclude_skills.description: Skills the user does NOT want to work with (e.g. ['WordPress', 'Magento']).

tools.name: similar_jobs
tools.description: Find PHP jobs SIMILAR to a given reference job using MoreLikeThis search across title, required_skills and description fields. Use this when the user expresses interest in a specific job and wants alternatives — e.g. 'show me more jobs like this one' or 'what else is comparable?'. Returns active jobs ranked by similarity, excluding the reference job itself.

limit.description: Number of similar jobs to return.

tools.name: market_insights
tools.description: Market analysis for a specific tech stack / skill (Laravel, Symfony, WordPress, Shopware, TYPO3, ...): total active jobs, salary by experience level (junior/mid/senior/lead with avg_min and avg_max in EUR/year), top 10 cities with job count and avg max salary, remote/hybrid/onsite distribution, top 5 verified (claimed) employers, plus count of additional employers without a verified profile. Use this for market overview questions like 'how is the Laravel market looking right now?' or 'is Symfony in demand in Munich?'. The employer list in this overview contains verified employers only; other employers are counted. Employer names of individual jobs are always included in search_jobs / get_job results.

skill.description: Tech stack / framework (e.g. Laravel, Symfony, WordPress, Shopware, TYPO3, Magento, Drupal)

city.description: Optional city filter — restricts analysis to one city.
